Learning at New Anmol

Learning is a conversation, not simply a lecture.

Students are placed at the centre of the learning process—developing ideas, opinions, critical thinking and active responsibility for their academic journey.

Student-centred learningPractical learningProfessional preparationResearch-informed teachingFaculty

Teaching & learning

“Students are encouraged to become independent, self-motivated learners who take active responsibility for their academic journey.”
01

Student-centred

Students develop their own ideas, opinions and critical-thinking abilities through an active learning process.

02

Independent

Learners are encouraged to take responsibility for their progress from the beginning of their course.

03

Engaging

Faculty knowledge, enthusiasm and passion for teaching shape a dynamic academic environment.

04

Purposeful

Learning moves beyond understanding concepts towards applying knowledge in professional settings.

Practical learning

Understanding theory through hands-on experience.

Practical learning connects theoretical concepts with the tools, environments and skills students will encounter in professional healthcare practice.

Laboratories and learning facilities support demonstrations, guided practice and applied understanding. Different programmes provide different learning settings as students progress through their courses.

Explore laboratories →

Professional preparation

Qualities for study, work and responsibility.

As students gain greater control of their learning, they are encouraged to develop qualities that support future professional practice.

01

Creativity

Developing ideas and approaching unfamiliar challenges thoughtfully.

02

Independence

Taking active responsibility for learning and continued development.

03

Teamwork

Learning to contribute, communicate and work with others.

04

Goal setting

Connecting academic progress with clear personal and professional objectives.

05

Problem solving

Applying knowledge and critical thinking to practical situations.

Research-informed teaching

Practical, current and future-oriented.

Research and teaching are integrated so students gain knowledge that is practical and up to date.

This approach keeps courses connected with developments in healthcare and supports an education that remains relevant, dynamic and oriented towards professional practice.
